assumptions: Every reachable vertex is a key in the adjacency dictionary (the code indexes self.vertices[vertex]); start_vertex is valid; adjacency lists are the graph representation; each adjacency entry counts toward E; set operations and queue put/get are expected/amortized O(1).
input_size: V = number of reachable vertices; E = adjacency entries scanned from reachable vertices; n = V + E.
rationale: Time: BFS marks a vertex visited before enqueueing, so each reachable vertex is enqueued and removed once. Its adjacency list is scanned once; total work is O(V + E). Score with n = V + E. Auxiliary space: The visited set and queue contain at most O(V) reachable vertices. The returned visited set is the result; counting it as working storage does not change the O(V) bound. Owner review: Confirmed against source: visited.add occurs in the same branch as queue.put, so every reachable vertex is enqueued once at most. Every reachable adjacency entry is scanned once; time O(V + E), space O(V), and the queue holds at most V vertices.

assumptions: Score the bottom-up entrypoint only; character comparison and table access are O(1); m and k may independently be zero or larger; N=max(m,k); retain boundary-cell work in the exact bound.
input_size: m = len(word1); k = len(word2); N = max(m, k).
rationale: Time: The implementation fills every cell of an (m+1) by (k+1) table, including boundary rows and columns. The complete bound is O((m+1)(k+1)); this remains valid when either input is empty. With N=max(m,k), the worst-case class is O(N^2). Auxiliary space: The implementation allocates an (m+1) by (k+1) table. The complete space bound is O((m+1)(k+1)), including empty-input cases; its worst case for N=max(m,k) is O(N^2). Owner review: Confirmed against source: the full (m+1) by (n+1) table is allocated and every cell is filled, including boundaries for empty strings. Time and space are O((m+1)(k+1)), worst case O(N^2). For the label, k = len(word2); the code names the second length n.

assumptions: Character access is O(1); treat ArrayList append as amortized O(1); k>0 for a non-early-return run; matching output is excluded from auxiliary space; the helper computePrefixFunction is part of the analyzed operation.
expected_auxiliary_space_exact: O(k) auxiliary, excluding the returned occurrence list
input_size: m = haystack length; k = needle length; N = m + k.
rationale: Time: The prefix-function construction is O(k). In the matching pass, q only advances with the scan and fallback steps are amortized over prior advances, so the pass is O(m). Total O(m+k); score with N=m+k. Auxiliary space: The prefix-function array has k entries and matching uses scalar indices. The occurrence list is returned output and is excluded from auxiliary-space scoring. Owner review: Confirmed against source: the KMP scan and computePrefixFunction are amortized linear; pi uses O(k) space, excluding returned matches. For the label, k = needle.length; the code names it n. After a full match, q resets below n, keeping needle.charAt(q) in bounds.

assumptions: a is non-empty because the implementation reads a[0]; integer arithmetic is treated as O(1); n=a.length.
rationale: Time: The enhanced for-loop visits each array element once and performs constant work per element. Initialization and final comparison are constant time. Auxiliary space: Only the scalar variables sum and runningSum are added; no input-sized data structure is allocated. Owner review: Confirmed against source: one pass with scalar state gives O(n) time and O(1) space. The final predictedAnswer comparison is constant work. The non-empty assumption is required because the code reads a[0].

assumptions: Input is a Python string; dictionary operations are expected O(1); n is its length and U is the number of distinct characters.
input_size: n = len(input_string); U = number of distinct characters in it.
rationale: Time: The for-loop visits each character once. Dictionary lookup/update is expected O(1), and left only moves forward; total time is O(n). Auxiliary space: The character-index dictionary stores at most one entry for each distinct character seen, so it uses O(U) space, bounded by O(n). Owner review: Confirmed against source: left only moves forward, so the scan is O(n) expected time with expected O(1) dictionary operations. The map holds at most U distinct characters, so auxiliary space is O(U), U <= n. Type checking and the empty-string guard are O(1).
